I've been running Ubuntu, Debian, Mandriva, maybe a few others in there, since I got my free Warty CD's in the mail. I've had a serious love/hate affair with those flavors of Linux over the years, and I must say that overall, I have to give it all a big "meh" based on my experiences as a whole.

After a bug with the nvidia driver left my home machine crippled for over a year (OK, bugzilla said it was a driver issue, then it was a kernel issue, then it was an X issue, then it went back to a driver issue) I finally gave up and switched to a R9-380X card (my christmas present to myself.) It was (and still is) absolutely amazing... it just worked, and worked fine, with no errors or tweaking or safe mode or profanity or anything else. Beautiful!

I'm currently running 14.04, and it is ok, but not nearly as good as 12.04 imho. I've noticed over the years that Ubuntu tends to be a lot like Windows in that their LTS releases follow the same pattern as Windows... every second one is good. 8 was fantastic, 10 was wishy-washy, 12 was fantastic, 14 is... well, it follows the pattern.

Silly as it sounds, I was actually looking forward to 16 until I found out there is no longer a driver for my card other than the generic driver included on the iso. No, thanks.

Today, I see that there is finally a driver for 16.04, and I am anxious to give it a try! Fortunately, it is a 4-day weekend for me, so I should have time to update to 16, get it running, and play around a little.

So at lunch today, I downloaded the iso as well as the driver, and put them on a thumb drive.

Just so I could take a look, I tried the thumb drive on my company laptop, a Lenovo Thinkpad W530; our engineering department has about two dozen engineers with W530's, and our attempt at using Linux a few years ago was disastrous, so I was hoping to see if it is any better.

Installation stops cold and bitches about not being able to set the clock (same as in 2014, same with Debian.)

After a few re-boots and re-tries, it will finally get passed that error and get to a desktop.

Then, if the screen blanks after a time-out, or if the screen is closed for any amount of time, any key will wake it up and bring me back to a desktop, but then the OS freezes. Totally. And I mean no key strokes will work at all - that includes reisub. Nothing. (This is also unchanged from the last time I tried on a w530.) This behavior repeats on 2 W530's, so I am assuming it is the same on all of them. And I say the OS freezes, because Fn/Spacebar still cycles the back-lit keyboard and overhead light with no problem... hmmm.

I never did get a chance to see if the logitech mouse driver issue was fixed, but the fact that the clock is still an issue at boot, and that the system hangs when a laptop lid is closed or if the screen power-saving setting kicks in, then I really don't know if I want to risk my home machine.
